A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dropout Decoding research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite the changed title, layout, and additional material.

before.justification: v1 reports original CHAIR, THRONE, and MMBench evaluations, decoding ablations, and generated-caption examples in Sections 6–7 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds computational-cost measurements, masking comparisons, and masked-token statistics.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains text-space projection, epistemic uncertainty estimation, optional relevant-token retention, uncertainty-guided dropout, and majority voting. Sections 4–5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same components; the new masking variants are experimental controls.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MSCOCO image captioning using CHAIR and THRONE, plus MMBench. The additional analyses retain this coverage. Specifying the MSCOCO 2014 test set in v2 documents the existing evaluation rather than establishing a newly added dataset.

E2.justification: v2 Section 7.5 adds high-confidence token masking as an evaluated comparison variant. Greedy decoding, beam search, OPERA, and VCD remain the main baselines. Random masking was already evaluated in v1 Appendix C, so its appearance in the main text is not a wholly new comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds BLEU to the masking comparison and measurements of throughput, latency per 50 tokens, and memory. Appendix B corrects gamma(k) from 0.2k+1 to 0.2k+0.1, matching v1's main-text values. The MMBench token limit changes from 1 to 256 in the settings table, but the prose still says 1; this reported inconsistency does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The supporting analyses expand substantially: v2 adds the high-confidence-masking control, measured computational overhead, and average masked-token counts. The existing random-masking analysis gains quantitative CHAIR/BLEU comparisons and THRONE evaluation failures in Section 7.4. The candidate-count and preliminary-pass ablations remain, rather than being newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 already reports uncertainty values in Table 1 and standard deviations in Figure 3. v2 Appendix B newly specifies averages and standard deviations across three random seeds associated with sampling 500 images. This clarifies the reporting procedure without establishing an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 3 retain their results, but v2 adds substantial diagnostic and computational evidence: masking-control scores, masked-token counts, and throughput of 37.0/34.1/20.1 tokens/s for greedy/without/with preliminary passes. v1's repetition-frequency estimate of 20–25 cases out of 500 disappears. New Table 4 also reports LLaVA-1.5 greedy CHAIR_I as 7.90, conflicting with 12.83 in the retained Table 1.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, decoding equations, uncertainty decomposition, and Appendix A derivation are retained. The new masking discussion supplies empirical interpretation, not an additional theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-free visual-token uncertainty estimation and dropout-based ensemble decoding to reduce hallucinations and improve reliability. The added analyses support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 corrects the preliminary-pass recommendation: models with more visual tokens, rather than fewer as stated at the end of v1 Section 7.2, may benefit from skipping it. It adds explanations of high-confidence masking and misleading CHAIR improvements under repetitive generation, and explicitly identifies dependence on text-space projection quality as a limitation.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents the MSCOCO 2014 test split, 500-image sampling, and evaluation prompt. Section 7.1 adds hardware and implementation information, including four A800 80GB GPUs, vLLM, Transformers, batching, and KV caching. Appendix B corrects the dropout hyperparameter formula, while v1's explicit random-masking probability specification is lost. The code-access statement is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of AGLA and Memory-Space Visual Retracing and removes the CDG discussion. Section 4 newly connects text-space projection to logit lens, citing Belrose et al. Introductory citations are also refreshed, but the central research positioning remains similar; the newly discussed methods are not evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title, updates affiliations, condenses several introductory and explanatory passages, and converts contribution bullets into prose. Ablation headings are revised, the random-masking discussion moves into the main text, and limitations, an impact statement, and a checklist are added. The overall narrative and section progression remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a two-column layout to a single-column NeurIPS format. Existing figures, tables, and example panels are substantially resized and repositioned, with several displays becoming smaller. New Tables 3–5 and 9 present efficiency, masking comparisons, and masked-token counts; the existing benchmark displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the unchanged method easier to assess through measured inference costs, the high-confidence-masking control, clearer seed reporting, and corrected implementation and interpretation details. These address gaps in v1's supporting evidence. The gains are tempered by new inconsistencies in the MMBench token budget and the greedy CHAIR_I value in Table 4, so the overall improvement is limited.
